title: EMBGuard: Constructing Hazard-Aware Guardrails for Safe Planning in Embodied Agents
evidence: Non-adversarial physical hazards; no attacker/jailbreak mentioned -> NA. Fine-tuned Qwen3-VL 2B/4B guard R:(image I, action a)->(risk, type, hazard expl.) before execution; judge sees environment visual observation (coded exposed). IS-Bench downstream: 'Conditioned on the guardrail feedback and the task context, the policy model proposes a next action, which is expected to mitigate the identified risk' (no hard block described). Policies GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen3-VL-32B; step acc./precision 92.1/recall 61.5 only, no task success. Latency 0.535s(2B)/0.719s(4B). Benign-scenario false positives in Fig.6. v1 date from citation metadata (abs history not rendered).

title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
evidence: Non-adversarial incidents ('unintended behaviors can emerge even when individual actions appear harmless'); no adaptive attacks. DSL rule = trigger (deterministic tool match) + NL check 'interpreted by the agent' over env state, latest observation, recent context; post-step detection -> containment/recovery actions + task termination (also post); eradication synthesizes guardrail rules checked on the plan, 'blocks the corresponding action before any tool invocation'. Rules developer-authored + LLM-synthesized. GPT-5 only. Check 6.9-11.7s; safe-task overhead 1.40-1.44x; 0 FP on 50 SafeAgentBench + 35 OSWorld safe tasks; no with/without utility comparison.

title: FormalJudge: A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight
evidence: Post-hoc oversight of completed trajectory tau vs intent I: LLM decomposes intent into atomic constraints and extracts facts from trajectory (actions + observations o_t); Dafny/Z3 proves compliance -> binary verdict. Adversary = deceptive overseen agent (upward deception); Deceivers built with 'GPT-4.1 as the attacker LLM to systematically inject constraint violations'; L1-L4 deception levels target agent traces, none designed to fool the judge -> 0. Iterative refinement: agents receive verification results and regenerate (70.7%->99.8%). 7 agents (GPT-4o, Gemini-3.0-Pro, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, Qwen2.5 7/14/32/72B), 5 judge models. No cost/latency; no FPR breakout; labels by 3-LLM majority vote.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Enhancing Agent Behavioral Safety with Thought Correction
evidence: Separate fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B 'edits each intermediate thought before action execution' from (instruction, history of thoughts+observations, current thought); safe thoughts passed unchanged (I-T-T warm-up). Stated focus 'behavioral safety... rather than explicit jailbreak attempts' but evaluated on AgentDojo/InjecAgent injection and AgentHarm; no attack on the aligner itself -> 0. 6 backbones (GPT-4.1, o3, Claude-Sonnet-4, Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-3.3-70B); helpfulness reported (e.g. AgentDojo DeepSeek-V3 safety 97.1%/helpful 34.4%); ~0.11s/step. fpr = thought-level precision 96.3% on validation set only, no benign-task over-refusal metric. Coded A (step-level thought correction pre-action).

title: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Compliance
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.03485 (latest arXiv HTML, ICML 2026 title; v1 titled 'Towards Policy-Compliant Agents: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Policy Violation Detection')
evidence: Non-adversarial policy violations; no attackers/injection mentioned. PolicyGuard-4B (Qwen3-4B SFT) labels policy + trajectory actions (no page observations) violation/no_violation, full-trajectory and prefix (N=1..5). Closed-loop replay: interceptor 'checks proposed agent actions... before execution. When a potential violation is detected, the guardrail blocks the action and triggers a retry'; CuP 10.20%->16.33%, 71.97% block on violating proposals; agent backbone unspecified. Policies GPT-4o-synthesized + curated, given as judge input (no RULE). 22.5 ms/example, 2.57 TFLOPs. fpr weak: FP share only (9.7% of 1,091 errors on 12k test); no false-block rate in deployment. v1 date from secondary metadata.

title: Firewalls to Secure Dynamic LLM Agentic Networks
evidence: Malicious external agent (privacy extraction, manipulation, injection). Language Converter Firewall: LLM converts incoming external-agent message to JSON, then 'Programmatic verifier... entirely deterministic; no LLM involved' strips non-conforming fields + anonymizes (converter LLM reads untrusted messages -> exposed Y). Data Abstraction Firewall: LLM with rules + raw user data only ('never observes external agent messages') abstracts/prohibits data before it reaches the assistant. Protocol/rules LLM-derived offline from demonstration corpora ('Learn the language from demonstrations') -> LEARN. Threat model says attacker 'can adaptively and dynamically probe' but eval uses ConVerse (Gomaa et al., 2026) 864 attacks, none firewall-aware -> 0. 4 models (GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash); utility coverage/rating reported; no overhead; no FPR. No tool-call firewall.

title: VeriSafe Agent: Safeguarding Mobile GUI Agent via Logic-based Action Verification
evidence: Non-adversarial LFM errors; no attacks mentioned. GPT-4o autoformalizes user instruction into DSL spec once before execution (P); deterministic logic engine verifies each action's developer-library-declared state transition 'before the agent's proposed UI actions are injected into a mobile app'; failures blocked with roadmap/soft/hard feedback to agent. Spec LLM-generated from instruction (trusted input only); state predicates developer-defined (MIX-leaning). Accuracy 94.33-98.33%, FPR 2.7%; task completion 40%->76%/92% (Challenge, M3A on GPT-4o); latency/cost vs steps in Fig.8 (near-constant). No user confirmation.
